Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:60: And to understand the difference between devikah [cleaving], chashikah [desire], and chafitzah [delight] - for if the matter were merely doubled in different words, this would not indicate [distinct degrees of] affection; rather, we must say that each of these terms indicates some aspect of affection that the others do not indicate.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:61: "Devikah" [cleaving] indicates a person's soul cleaving to the soul of his fellow, along the lines of (I Kings 1:12), "them [Adonijah's supporters] to whom Solomon cleaved" [in general company]; and likewise (Ruth 1:14), "and Ruth cleaved to her" - meaning, the cleaving of her will to her. However, this "cleaving" does not indicate unity to such a great extent, for it is still possible for what is cleaved to separate - and the proof is from the source from which our Rabbis, of blessed memory, learned cleaving: "as the belt cleaves to the loins of a man, so have I made cleave to Me the whole house of Israel," and so on, as explained above - and a belt is sometimes cleaved to a person and sometimes not cleaved, for he may loosen it from himself.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:62: However, the word "chashak" [desire] indicates a stronger bond of love - for we find that the Torah uses this word concerning the matter of binding and unity (Exodus 38:12), "and their bands [chashukeihem] of silver" - meaning fastened and attached, for the pillars had silver threads that were fastened and attached and bound around them, as is done with wooden barrels to fasten them - so the Radak explains in the root "chashak."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:63: "Chafetz" [delight/desire] is even more - that the will and entire intent of a person be toward her face, not moving from her even for one hour - along the lines of what is said (I Chronicles 28:9), "with a perfect heart and a willing [chafetzah] soul." And this is (Genesis 34:19), "and the young man did not delay to do the thing, because he delighted [chafetz] in Jacob's daughter" - he did not delay the matter, and it was as though he were dying of love for her, having no other will in the world but this one alone. And so too, the reality of union [marital relations] is designated in Scripture with the term "chefetz" - along the lines of (I Kings 10:13), "all her desire [chefetzah] that she asked," concerning the Queen of Sheba, which our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explain as referring to relations with her. And further, they explain in the Zohar (Yitro 89a), on the verse (Isaiah 56:4), "and choose the things that please [chafatzti] Me" - "that please Me," without qualification, refers to the union with the Matronita - the reason being that in union, all of a person's will, heart, and all his limbs are toward one face.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:64: And therefore, from the proofs brought in the discourse for "devikah" and "chashikah," we learn the understanding of the matter, that "chashikah" is greater than "devikah," and likewise "chafitzah" is greater than "chashikah." For "devikah," it brought the verse "but you who cleave" - you already know what I explained above, that this does not indicate so much the cleaving of the Holy One, blessed be He, to them, but rather that they are cleaved to Him. The second verse indicates greater affection: (Deuteronomy 7:7), "not because you were more numerous than all peoples did the LORD desire [chashak] you" - it appears that He, of Himself, desired them without their having first aroused any deed; but it does not indicate the affection so strongly, for our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explain (Chullin 89a): "not because you were more numerous" - the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel, I desire you, and so on, because the Holy One, blessed be He, gives you greatness while you diminish yourselves. The third verse (Malachi 3:12), "and all nations shall call you happy" - this is for the future to come - "for you shall be a delightful land" - it appears that this is a level they have not yet attained, but rather, "you shall be a delightful land" - and the explanation of "chefetz" is a term for "will" - that His will, blessed be He, is in us without any cause at all, but rather that His delight and will in them is out of abundant affection, like a person who delights in this land more than that one, even though they are equal.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:65: And in the manner we have explained, that these general categories correspond to nefesh, ruach, neshamah, the matter is settled - that each word indicates something in the matter of affection and love that the others do not indicate, as we explained above, that the aspect of love of the nefesh is not equal to the love of the ruach, nor the love of the ruach to the love of the neshamah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:66: It remains for us to explain a matter in the discourse that pertains greatly to the matter of love - namely, to know why the author of the discourse needed to bring all three from the passage concerning that wicked man. And we saw that it is a lengthy matter, so we will explain it in a chapter of its own, in order to give the reader some room to breathe.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:1: This chapter will explain the love of the Shechinah, and how our love for her should be, so that it cannot be separated. And this is the reality learned from the passage concerning that wicked man, and its explanation is according to what the commentators explain, particularly Rabbi Menachem Recanati, peace be upon him, who writes that Shechem, son of Chamor the Chivite, who came upon Dinah - his secret is the serpent that came upon Eve - and this is "Chivi," a term related to "chivya" [serpent, in Aramaic]. And Dinah, it is already known what they explain in the Zohar, that she is "the law of the kingdom is law" [dina de-malchuta dina] - meaning that Leah, the supernal Imma, bore six sons and one daughter, and this daughter is the Shechinah, and she is Din [judgment], as is known. And since that wicked man, because of sin, cleaved his soul to Dinah, daughter of Jacob, in cleaving, in desire, and in delight - so too it is fitting for a person that his soul cleave to the Shechinah in these three realities, as we shall explain.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:2: And this was also the intent of the author of the discourse in bringing the three terms of affection with which the Holy One, blessed be He, held Israel dear - to show us that, just as He so desires to cleave to us, so it is fitting that we cleave to Him in these three aspects. And of this the Torah commanded and said (Leviticus 19:18), "and you shall love your neighbor as yourself" - and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, already explained (Shemot Rabbah 27:1; Zohar, Beshalach 55b) that "your neighbor" [re'acha] is the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said (Proverbs 27:10), "do not forsake your friend [re'acha] and your father's friend." And further, the Holy One, blessed be He, out of His abundant love for us, calls us "friends" [re'im], as it is said (Psalms 122:8), "for the sake of my brothers and my friends"; and likewise (ibid. 148:14), "for the children of Israel, a people near to Him." Therefore it says, "and you shall love your neighbor as yourself" - "your neighbor," who is the Holy One, blessed be He; "as yourself" - with the love that you desire for yourself. Just as if you have a friend, you desire that he love you, so the Holy One, blessed be He, who is your neighbor, wants you to love Him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:3: And further, the intent of "as yourself" is this: it is known to us that if there are two friends who love one another, and one of them, out of his abundant love for his fellow, did good to him and clothed him and fed him and gave him drink and other benefits - it is only right that his fellow not be ungrateful, but rather love him as his own soul; and if it should happen that the friend who did him good needs something, it is fitting that this one, who already received from his fellow, repay that kindness according to his ability - and if he has no ability, he should at least show his good heart toward him and that he has nothing with which to repay his debt to him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:4: And so too is the matter of the allegory: that the Holy One, blessed be He, preceded His goodness to every creature, and especially to His people Israel, through several miracles and wonders He did and does for us, as we shall speak of this further below. And therefore it is fitting that a person recognize the goodness of the Holy One, blessed be He, who is his friend, and love Him, so as not to be ungrateful, and so on, as they explain in the Tikkunim several times (see 37a); and one must perform acts of loving-kindness with Him and with His Shechinah through the deeds of Torah and the commandments, for (Proverbs 27:8), "as a bird that wanders from its nest, so is a man who wanders from his place." And concerning the matter of acts of loving-kindness, we will copy the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, below. And at every time, the reality of love should never be lacking, for (Deuteronomy 10:12), "what does the LORD ask of you but to fear and to love" - for fear and love are in the heart and soul, and these are things within your own body, which you need not seek from another - and this is "from you"; and so it says elsewhere (ibid. 30:14), "for the matter is very near to you, in your mouth and in your heart, to do it."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:5: And according to this explanation, "your neighbor" applies both to the righteous man and to the Shechinah. And we find support for this in the words of Rashbi (Zohar, Terumah 169b), concerning the sixth of the seven blessings recited for the bridegroom and bride, which is "make the beloved friends greatly rejoice" - and they say, of blessed memory: "Tzaddik" and "Tzedek" are "friends and beloved," who never separate one from the other - to this point. And since we find that both together are called "friends," it implies that each one, by itself, may be called "your neighbor" without qualification - and this is not a strange matter, for we already find in the Gemara that the female is called "your neighbor." Our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Kiddushin 41a): Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav, it is forbidden for a man to betroth a woman until he has seen her, lest he see something repulsive in her and come to hate her - and the Merciful One says, "and you shall love your neighbor as yourself" - to this point. Behold, the female too is included in "and you shall love your neighbor."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:6: And concerning "and you shall love your neighbor" as referring to the righteous man, it is possible to say it in another way, along the lines of what is explained in the words of Rashbi (Zohar, Vayechi 216a), concerning the matter of "the righteous shall inherit the land"; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:7: And concerning "your neighbor" as referring to the Shechinah, it is possible to explain it in another way as well, through what was explained above (chapter 3, from Zohar, Bereshit 51a) concerning the matter of "but you who cleave to the LORD your God" - that Israel cleave to that blue fire, so that they are the wick to which the fire holds; and just as that fire needs oil in order to burn, and if not, it is extinguished - so this holy fire that rests upon our heads, "for the LORD your God is a consuming fire" (Deuteronomy 4:24), its "consuming" is Torah, prayer, and the commandments, which are the oil supplied - and this is (Ecclesiastes 9:8), "let your garments always be white, and let your head lack no oil." And so it is explained in the words of Rashbi, of blessed memory (Zohar, Parashat Balak 187a): he opened and said (Ecclesiastes 2:14), "the wise man's eyes are in his head," and so on - and is there any other place for a person's eyes but in his head? Rather, perhaps it means in his body, or in his arm, which brings forth the wise man more than all the people of the world? Rather, the verse is certainly this: for we have learned, a person should not walk four cubits bareheaded - why? Because the Shechinah rests upon his head; and everyone whose eyes and words are wise, they are in that which rests and stands over his head. And when his eyes are there, he should know that this light that is kindled over his head needs oil - because a person's body is the wick, and the light is kindled above - and King Solomon cried out and said, "and let oil not be lacking on your head" - "on your head," for the light that is on his head needs oil, which is good deeds - and therefore, "the wise man's eyes are in his head," and not in another place - to this point. And in the Tikkunim (page 60b), it says that Israel are the wick, the Torah is the oil, and the Shechinah is the lamp - this is what is written (Job 29:3), "when His lamp shone upon my head" - to this point. And along these lines, the verse "and let oil not be lacking on your head" is explained: that one should give oil, which is the Torah, to the lamp that is on his head.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:8: And through this the verse may be understood (Isaiah 62:6), "you who remind the LORD, take no rest" - because their arousal depends on those below, as explained in the Song of Songs [passage] and in several places. And my teacher, peace be upon him, explained that this is what David meant when he said (Psalms 30:13), "so that glory may sing praise to You and not be silent; O LORD my God, I will give thanks to You forever" - "glory" [kavod] is the Shechinah, and in order for her to sing praise above and not be silent, I too, below, must always give thanks to You.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:9: And through this we may understand "and you shall love your neighbor as yourself" - meaning, that you should love the Shechinah, giving her the arousal of deeds always, so that she never be lacking - just as you desire for yourself; for it is known that she is the mother who flows to those below the flow of life and goodness, and just as you desire and love that life and flow never be lacking to you for a moment, so you should love to give oil above, as I explained - for the upper ones need the lower ones - and this is what they said, of blessed memory: the Shechinah dwelling among those below is a need of the One on high - as my teacher, peace be upon him, explained this matter at length in the book Pardes Rimonim.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:10: And along these lines, concerning the reality of devikah, chashikah, and chafitzah - we must love the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah in all three, just as we desire that the Holy One, blessed be He, love us in all three - for there is no complete love except in all three; and this is a fourth explanation concerning the matter of "and you shall love your neighbor as yourself."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:11: And let us return to the exposition and understanding of the discourse, which we said - that what the author of the discourse brought, all three of which we learn from the passage concerning that wicked man, is to teach us that a person is obligated to love the Shechinah in all three. And the reason is that it is impossible for the Shechinah to be unified above unless the righteous man first has these three aspects toward her, and then, through these three, the Shechinah cuts a covenant with him, because through him she is made into a vessel, as we shall explain - and they explain, of blessed memory (Sanhedrin 22b), that a woman cuts a covenant only with one who makes her into a vessel [i.e., consummates the marriage].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:12: The first, "in cleaving," as it is said (Genesis 34:3), "and his soul cleaved to Dinah" - the reality of cleaving is that a person's soul should cleave and direct his whole intent to unify the Shechinah and separate from her all the husks, and likewise to separate from his own thought all extraneous thoughts, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Vayelech 285a) - for at the time of unification, one must unify the Shechinah in thought without any admixture of chaff and straw, and we copied this discourse in the last chapter of the Gate of Fear. And this is "and his soul cleaved to Dinah" - meaning, to this one, who is Dinah, he cleaves, and not to another at all - and just as it is true what they explain, of blessed memory (Nedarim 20b), that one should not drink from this cup and set his eye on another cup, and one [who does] is called "a son of exchange" - and how strict Rashbi is about this (Zohar, Vayetze 155a, in the Tosefta) - along these lines too, one's intention must not stray from the Shechinah and think of the filth of his thoughts, which are external, for then he would be found separating, Heaven forfend; rather, he should cleave to the Shechinah properly and separate everything else from her.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:13: And further, one who loves two women, their love in him is not complete, for they are rivals to one another; and in order for a wife's love to be firmly fixed in her husband, it is when she sees that he loves no other woman in the world but her alone - then she will cut with him a complete covenant of love. So too, the Shechinah will not bind her love to a person who loves the affairs of the world; and therefore the essence of love is that a person love nothing in the world more than his love of Him, blessed be He, and that his love of Him, blessed be He, exceed his love of his wife and children and the other affairs of the world. For what causes a person to be separated from love of the Holy One, blessed be He, while standing in prayer or occupied with Torah, so that evil, extraneous thoughts come to him, is because he is not fixed in love of the Holy One, blessed be He, with a love exceeding the affairs of this world - he loves both this and that, when he ought not to love the affairs of this world more than love of the Holy One, blessed be He. And since the Holy One, blessed be He, sees that his love of Him is not as it should be, and the person abandons Him, the Holy One, blessed be He, is also abandoned and separated from him - along the lines of the verse (I Chronicles 28:9), "if you seek Him, He will be found by you; but if you forsake Him, He will cast you off forever" - and then evil thought rules over him. Therefore one must separate love of this world, which is love of strangers and love of raisin-cakes (Hosea 3:1), for all these are external, and let his heart cleave to holy love, like Dinah, daughter of Jacob.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:14: And behold, through what I have explained, one doubt in this matter is resolved: for most of the verses in the Torah indicate "and to Him shall you cleave" - meaning, to Him, who is the Tree of Life, shall you cleave - and here we say it is a commandment to cleave to her [the Shechinah]. Rather, the matter is that this cleaving is only to exclude cleaving to another - along the lines of "and his soul cleaved to Dinah" and not to another - as we explained, that the intent is to separate the externality and everything else.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:15: And further, at the very beginning of entering [into prayer or a commandment], the cleaving must be to her, along the lines of "with this [bezot] shall Aaron come into the holy place" (Leviticus 16:2), which is explained in the Tikkunim (21b) - and it is explained there that everyone who performs a commandment, or prays, or occupies himself with Torah, should first direct his intent toward the Shechinah, to unify her. And therefore Rashbi, of blessed memory, explains (Tikkunim 33b): come and see, if a person, in his thought during his prayer, ascends to the Shechinah, or in every single commandment he performs - immediately, when he knocks at the gate of the King's Heichal, [whether he is] a prophet, a seer, a sage, or a righteous man - immediately, when he calls at the gate, if the Shechinah ascends there, YHVH answers immediately, and does not wait for a servant or an officer to open, but rather He Himself opens for him, out of the affection and love He has for him, like a bridegroom toward a bride. But if the Shechinah does not ascend in that prayer or commandment, the Holy One, blessed be He, does not consider it worth opening His Heichal for him, even through a messenger, and he is not worthy to enter the King's Heichal, and of him it is said, "you shall stand outside," and from outside they give him his requests through a messenger or an officer; and if his prayer does not ascend properly, they push him back outside and close the gates before him, and of him it is said (Proverbs 1:28), "then they shall call me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me." And so, when each and every one of Israel calls upon the Holy One, blessed be He, in the reading of the Shema, or in prayer, or in any commandment - if the Shechinah is not there, [the response] does not descend there - this is what is written (Exodus 20:21), "in every place where I cause My name to be remembered, I will come to you and bless you" - and Onkelos translates, "in every place where I cause My Shechinah to dwell," and so on - for when a person raises the Shechinah through his commandments toward the Holy One, blessed be He, the Holy One, blessed be He, descends upon him because of her. And therefore the prophet says (Jeremiah 9:23), "let him not glory," and so on, "but only in this let him who glories glory" - and this has already been established - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:16: Behold, it is explained in the discourse that the Holy One, blessed be He, literally opens for him out of the affection and love He has for her; and to this, a person must direct his whole intent to unify the Shechinah - and correspondingly, this is cleaving to her, and this is "and his soul cleaved to Dinah," "and he loved the young woman," and "he spoke to the heart of the young woman" - all these are preparations for unification. But the wicked man did the reverse order - he lay with her and violated her, and afterward "his soul cleaved" - and this is not the proper order; rather, first "his soul cleaved to Dinah" - meaning, to this one and not to another - and afterward that he cleave to her in love, and speak to her words that comfort the heart, and afterward desire [chesheck], and afterward delight [chafetz], as we shall explain.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:17: Further, there is another matter in cleaving, which is found concerning Ruth, when Boaz said to her (Ruth 2:8), "have you not heard, my daughter? Do not go to glean in another field, and also do not pass from here, but cleave here to my maidens" - this indicates two aspects: the first, "turn from evil," meaning "do not glean in another field" - for "another" [acher], without qualification, is Samael, other gods; and the second, "and cleave here to my maidens."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:18: And so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explain in the Pesikta, in these words: "do not go to glean in another field" - alluding to "you shall have no other gods." "And also do not pass from here" - alluding to (Exodus 20:3), "this is my God, and I will glorify Him." "And cleave here" - (Deuteronomy 4:4), "but you who cleave." "To my maidens" [na'arotai] - these are the righteous, who are called "youths" [ne'arim], as it is said (Job 40:29), "will you play with him as with a bird, or will you bind him for your maidens [na'arotayich]?" - to this point. This explicitly teaches everything expounded. And it says, concerning the matter of cleaving, two aspects: the first, "but you who cleave," according to its plain sense, as is known; the second, that in order to cleave to her, one must cleave to the righteous - as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, expound (see Bamidbar Rabbah 22:1), on "and to Him shall you cleave" - is it possible to cleave to the Shechinah? Is it not already said, "for the LORD your God is a consuming fire"? Rather, one should cleave to the righteous.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:19: And it is possible to say, in the way of the Zohar, that "maidens" without qualification refers to the seven maidens explained several times (Zohar, Pekudei 260b) - for what is said, "and cleave here to my maidens," means to cleave the attribute of Koh [the letters kaf-heh, representing Malchut] with the seven maidens fitting to be given to her from the King's house, which are the seven holy Heichalot, explained by Rashbi, peace be upon him, in Parashat Pekudei (244b), where it is explained how the Heichalot are set in order in the order of prayer for the repair of the Shechinah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:20: And along these lines, "and he spoke to her heart" refers to the blessings of the reading of the Shema, which are her adornments - particularly in the blessing of love [Ahavah], which ascends to the Heichal of Love, and there, through this blessing, we arouse a placation and appeasement toward the Holy One, blessed be He, that He come to unite with her - as they explain in the Tikkunim (45a): woe to those people whose hearts and eyes are sealed, who do not strive to know the honor of their Master, to appease Him with His Shechinah through several supplications and appeasements, to bring Him down to the Shechinah - and all the more so to arouse love toward her, as they instituted, "who chooses His people Israel in love" - to this point. And the intent is that "His people Israel" are the souls of Israel included within her, for she is called the Community of Israel, and the Holy One, blessed be He, chooses her and them in love - for it is the way of the husband to love his wife, the wife of his youth, as it is said (Isaiah 54:6), "and a wife of youth, when she is rejected."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:21: And above this matter they explain that in "Shema Yisrael" we call to Israel, [meaning] Tiferet, and He comes to unite with her; in these words (Tikkunim 45a): another interpretation, (Exodus 32:18), "the sound of singing [anot] I hear" - this is the affliction [inuy] of "I" [Anochi, i.e., the Shechinah], who cries out every day to her husband, she and her children, and calls to Him twice, evening and morning, "Shema Yisrael." And every person who has affliction from the Shechinah, who is afflicted in exile, far from her husband, and calls to Him every day, "Shema Yisrael," that He descend to her - certainly of him it is said, "the sound of singing I hear" - the voice of that afflicted one, I hear - to this point. Behold, all this is consolation and speaking to her heart, by which she is somewhat comforted from the exile.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:22: And just as the incident of Shechem with Dinah occurred at a time of exile, when the moon was not in its proper repair, as explained in the Song of Songs [passage], until Moses came; and further, Jacob our father, peace be upon him, was away from his home - for had he been in the place of his fathers, in Beer Sheva, this incident would not have happened to him - and that wicked man did these three things to her, as explained in the discourse - so now, while the Shechinah is in exile, a person must repair the Shechinah and appease her with these repairs: in cleaving, as we explained; in love; in speaking to her heart. And we will further elaborate below on the matter of her repairs and speaking to her heart, in other aspects. And further, concerning the matter of cleaving through the seven maidens, there is another distinction, which will be explained in the matter of Torah and prayer.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:23: "Chashikah" [desire] has two aspects, along the lines we explained for "devikah": the first, that after his soul cleaves to the Shechinah, in every single commandment he performs, he must perform it with desire and the burning of his heart in very great love - and this is the matter of "re'uta de-liba" [the desire of the heart], which they explain in the Zohar several times (Yitro 93b); and it is impossible for "re'uta de-liba," which is this desire, unless thought of the Blessed Name and love of Him come first - and from the side of love, this desire is born.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:24: And the matter of this desire, which is "re'uta de-liba," is explained in the words of Rashbi, of blessed memory (Zohar, Shemot 198b): "take from among yourselves an offering for the LORD; every one whose heart makes him willing shall bring it" (Exodus 35:5). Come and see: at the time a person sets his will toward the service of his Master, that will first ascends upon the heart, which is the foundation and root of the whole body; afterward that good will ascends upon the limbs of the body, and the will of all the limbs of the body and the will of the heart join together as one, and they draw upon themselves the radiance of the Shechinah to dwell with them, and that person becomes the portion of the Holy One, blessed be He - just as it says, "take from among yourselves an offering" - "from among yourselves" was a drawing, to receive upon yourselves that offering, to become a portion for the LORD. And should you say that this matter is not within a person's control - come and see what is written, "every one whose heart makes him willing shall bring the offering of the LORD" - "every one whose heart makes him willing," certainly - whoever wills his heart draws the Shechinah to himself; this is what is written, "shall bring it" - even though she is in ascent above, he shall bring her from the supernal place, to draw her to dwell with him - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:25: And along these lines, our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explain, concerning the working of the inclination in man, in baraitot found in manuscript (in tractate Kallah, chapter 2), in these words: it is taught, a person's inclination grows stronger against him every day, as it is said (Genesis 6:5), "and every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil all the day." From here our Rabbis expounded: improper thought leads to desire, desire leads to love, love leads to pursuit, pursuit leads to action - to inform you how hard it is to turn back from one to the next. And correspondingly, in repentance: abstinence leads to watchfulness, watchfulness leads to alacrity - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:26: And for our subject, the matter of love: improper thought and desire are "devikah," and love and pursuit are "chashikah," which is "re'uta de-liba." And here we will copy below the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, on "re'uta de-liba" pursuing, and action is "chafetz" - for action is the ultimate purpose of the sought-after desire; and it follows that there is no pursuit except from within desire and love - and this is what he explained, that from the side of love, this desire is born.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:27: And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Terumah 128a) that the essential way by which a person acquires the Shechinah, that she rest upon him, is "re'uta de-liba" [the desire of the heart]. He says there that the husks rest upon a person for free and entice him to perform a deed so that they may come to dwell with him; and he says afterward, the spirit of the Holy One, blessed be He, is not so - rather, [it requires] complete payment and abundant, great striving, and the fixing of oneself, and the purification of one's dwelling, and the desire of one's heart and soul - and would that he be able to widen [his capacity] to make Him dwell with him - and with all this, that a person walk on a straight path, not turning to the right or the left; and if not, immediately He departs from him and distances Himself from him, and he cannot widen [his capacity for Him] as before. And therefore it is written, "and let them take for Me an offering, from every man" - from him who is called "ish" [man], one who overcomes his inclination - for whoever overcomes his inclination is called "ish" - "whose heart makes him willing [yidvenu]" - what is "whose heart makes him willing"? Rather, that his heart desire the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said (Psalms 27:8), "to You my heart says," "the rock of my heart" (ibid. 73:26), "and a good heart" (Proverbs 15:15), "and his heart was merry" (Ruth 3:7) - all of these are said concerning the Holy One, blessed be He. Here too, "whose heart makes him willing" - from him you shall take My offering, for there it is found and not in another place.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:28: And how do we know that the Holy One, blessed be He, desires him and makes His dwelling in him? When we see that that person's will is united with the desire of his heart, to pursue and strive after Him with his heart, his soul, and his will - certainly there we know that the Shechinah rests upon him, and then we must acquire that person with full payment - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:29: Behold, it is explained at the end of the discourse that the essence of everything is "re'uta de-liba," and this is the explanation of "whose heart makes him willing" - and he explains that this "re'uta de-liba" is the desire of the heart. And he says, "in re'uta de-liba, to pursue and strive after Him with his heart, his soul, and his will" - it appears that one should strive to pursue after the Holy One, blessed be He, and after His commandments, and cleave to Him with heart and soul and "re'uta de-liba," which is the burning of the heart that we explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:30: And the preceding preparations he mentioned, "complete payment" and "abundant, great striving," are all preparations for cleaving; and all this is included in the verse when it says "from every man" - as he wrote, that "ish" [man] is one who overcomes his inclination, and the preparations needed to overcome one's inclination are those mentioned at the beginning of the discourse, and they are what cause the cleaving, as I explained above, that it is impossible to cleave unless one separates the husks from himself, which is the subduing of the inclination.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:31: And the explanation of "complete payment" - it is possible that he intended the matter of "acquire for yourself a companion" (Avot 1:6), meaning acquire with payment. And "abundant, great striving" is the matter of "alacrity leads to the holy spirit," as we elaborated in explaining the discourse (Avodah Zarah 20b), "Rabbi Pinchas [ben Yair] says, watchfulness leads to alacrity." "The fixing of oneself" is the preparation of oneself, along the lines of "prepare to meet your God" (Amos 4:12), which is explained in Parashat Noach (Zohar 72a), and we copied his text in the Gate of Holiness. "The purification of one's dwelling" is "and your camp shall be holy" (Deuteronomy 23:15). "And the desire of his heart" is the desire of the heart. "That he walk on a straight path" - as King Solomon, peace be upon him, said (Proverbs 4:27), "do not turn to the right or the left" - and the explanation of "do not turn to the right" is along the lines of (Ecclesiastes 7:16), "do not be overly righteous," and "left" - "do not be overly wicked" - meaning, from the extremes, take the middle path. And it says, "one who is called 'ish,' who overcomes his inclination" - the intent is the subduing of all matters of matter [physicality], and the reason is that it is impossible for the light of the Shechinah to cleave to one who is physical, partnered with matters of matter, for the inclination will incline him toward matters of matter - but rather to one over whom the good inclination rules his evil inclination, for the good inclination is drawn from the side of the Shechinah, as we explained in the Gate of Fear, chapter 5 - and it follows that he is completely righteous, and therefore it is fitting that the Shechinah bind to him. And the desire is "his heart makes him willing" - "re'uta de-liba," as I explained - and this is that he desire his soul in the Shechinah, called "heart," as proven in the discourse "and a good heart" - and this matter applies rightly to all the commandments.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:32: And further, concerning the preparations needed to acquire the Shechinah for ourselves, we explained in chapter 6, in the discourse "your friend and your father's friend." And according to the second way we explained concerning cleaving, in the matter of prayer, that they are the seven maidens, which are the Heichalot - "chashikah," according to this, is the secret of the kisses performed in the Heichal of Ratzon [Will]; and I have already explained above, in chapter 2, that kisses are performed only out of abundant desire and affection.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:33: "Chafitzah" [delight], according to the way of unification explained in prayer, is the completion of unification in the secret of the Amidah - as Rashbi explains (Zohar, Terumah 128b), that when they juxtapose Redemption to the Amidah, the righteous man is aroused to join in the place needed, with love and affection, and so on, and the completion of unification is in "Sim Shalom" [the closing blessing]; and further, in falling upon one's face [tachanun], where one must give over his soul above for unification - and the completion of unification is called "chafetz," for this is the supernal will [chefetz] in unity. And further, all the preceding preparations for the union are vessels for the revelation of the "chefetz" [will/desire], for this was the beginning of the thought; however, it was not possible to reveal this "chefetz" except through the completion of all the aforementioned preparations - and this is along the lines of "the end of the deed is [rooted in] the beginning of the thought." And concerning the matter of the performance of the commandments, "chafitzah" is called the completion of the commandments, for this is the ultimate purpose and object of a person's will - the completion of the performance of the commandment with heart, soul, and body.
